newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt says coffee crop forecast unchanged. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt says coffee crop forecast unchanged. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Brazil's government has not changed its forecast for a 1997/98 coffee crop of 22 million 60-kg bags, the interim head of the National Coffee Department (Denac) said.

"Despite the private sector predicting a crop as low as 18 million bags (corrects from tonnes), we stick to our projection of a crop of 22 million bags," Roberto Abreu said, speaking through a spokeswoman.

Reports this week quoted "official sources" as saying the crop would only reach 20 million bags. But this was more likely to refer to the amount growers have been forecasting since before harvesting began.

"The harvest will be something in the range of 20 to 22 million bags, which is very far from the USDA's prediction of 28 million bags," said Hercilio Amaral Neto, executive secretary of the National Coffee Council (CNC), which represents growers.

Neto said reports appear to have originated from a short column item in a local newspaper, Estado de Sao Paulo, in which CNC vice-president Luis Suplicy Hafers was reported as saying that the crop would only reach 20 million bags.
The newspaper wrote, "The pessimistic forecasts regarding the Brazilian coffee crop are not coming true. 'But the more than pessimistic ones are,' coffee grower Luis Hafers said yesterday."

The article said Hafers made an ironic reference to the U.S. Department of Agriculture's controversial forecast for a 28 million bag crop. It quoted him as saying, "We're going to wait for instructions from the USDA now."
According to Neto, growers including Hafers have long been predicting the crop would reach 20 to 22 million bags.
"Luis was joking, he said we were going to ask the USDA to deliver us the difference," Neto said.
